notes: v660 - corrects the explanation given in v659, which blamed brokerage and was wrong at real position sizes. At $3 each way, brokerage is $6 whatever you invest: 1.2% of a $500 buy but only 0.12% of $5,000 and 0.06% of $10,000. So on any sensible size brokerage does NOT eat a 0.30% edge - it barely dents it. What eats it is the SPREAD, and that depends on the SHARE PRICE rather than on how much you put in. One ASX price step is half a cent from 10c up to $2, which is 2.9% of a 17-cent share but only 0.25% of a $2 one. The message now states brokerage as the small number it actually is and shows the spread cost for that particular share: for example 'Brokerage is only $6 (0.06%), but one price step on a $0.170 share is 2.9%, so crossing the spread costs about $294 in and out'. Same conclusion as before, but for the right reason - and it makes clear the problem is cheap shares, not small accounts. Display only; no scores or rules changed. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
